the following question: can we use deep learning to predict the deformations of a garment in 3D, as a function of the pose, shape and the style (geometry) of the garment, in a way that retains the high frequency components of the deformation?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose a novel approach for predicting 3D clothing deformation in a fully automatic and differentiable manner.
TailorNet is a novel approach that can generate realistic clothing deformations in 3D for different styles of clothing, shapes, and poses.
we present a new model for predicting clothing deformation in 2D as a function 3D pose, shape and garment style.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new model, which learns the deformation of a garment in 3D from a combination of pose, shape and garment style parameters.
we propose a new model that learns to predict the deformation of garments on humans in 3D.
we are the first to predict clothing deformation in 4D (pose x time) as a function of pose, shape and garment geometry, while retaining wrinkle details.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the physics based simulation of cloth deformation in 3d can be learned from a large number of static poses and a small number of dynamic ones.
the combination of neural networks, physics based simulations, and a decomposition of the problem into low and high frequency components can be used to learn a realistic 3D clothing model.
it is possible to learn physically plausible deformations from data alone, without the use of expensive and time consuming physics based simulation.
